description:
`jit issue reject --reason "<prose>"` writes a repository state that `jit validate` rejects, and neither documented repair path recovers it.

## Background

`jit issue reject` records its `--reason` as a `resolution:<reason>` label. A label must match `@/invariant/label-format` (`^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*:(?:[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._/-]*|...)$`), so any reason containing spaces, capitals, or punctuation produces a label that fails whole-repository validation.

The command warns but still commits the write, so the repository is left failing `jit validate` — and therefore failing the `repo-validate` gate — as the direct result of one documented invocation with a documented flag. Reproduced during epic `c639cfb5`:

```
$ jit issue reject 7793b8b7 --reason "Premise removed by 9a81ab12. ..."
Warning: [label-format] at raw_labels.2: "resolution:Premise removed by ..." is not valid
Rejected issue: 7793b8b7-...
$ jit validate
❌ Repository validation failed with 1 rule error(s)
```

Two further defects block recovery, which is what turns a bad write into a stuck state:

- `jit issue update <id> --remove-label "<the exact stored label>"` exits 0 and reports "Updated issue", but the label is still present afterwards. Passing the byte-exact string read from the issue's own JSON does not remove it, with or without `--force`. A caller cannot tell the no-op from a success.
- `jit validate --fix` reports "✓ No fixes needed" while `jit validate` on the same repository reports the error. The two disagree about whether the repository is valid.

Recovery required editing `.jit/issues/<id>.json` by hand and running `jit recover`, which is exactly what the CLI exists to make unnecessary.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A `--reason` that cannot form a valid label is refused before anything is written, naming the constraint, or is recorded somewhere that carries prose; no invocation leaves the repository failing `jit validate`.
- [hard] REQ-02: `--remove-label` removes the named label whenever it is present, including a label that does not satisfy the format rule, or it fails loudly; it never reports success without removing.
- [hard] REQ-03: `jit validate --fix` and `jit validate` agree on whether a repository is valid; `--fix` either repairs the finding or states that it cannot and why.
- [hard] REQ-04: Tests cover a reject reason that cannot form a label, removal of a malformed label, and the `--fix`/validate agreement.

## Notes

Found by dogfooding during epic `c639cfb5`; not part of that epic's scope. Whichever surface owns it should decide whether prose reasons belong in a label at all — the description or an event record carries prose without constraining it to a token vocabulary.
title: A reject reason can leave the repository failing validation
